description: Senior Security Codex assurance contracts. External controls require signed subject-bound attestations; KonnaxionDiag never treats documentation as evidence.

contracts.name: Separate Identity Planes
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: A principal is not a single string

contracts.name: Workload Identity by Trust Domain
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Long-lived service secrets are an implementation shortcut, not an identity architecture

contracts.name: Sender-Constrained Credentials
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Bearer tokens convert theft into authority: whoever possesses the token can use it until expiry

contracts.name: Explicit Delegation and Actor Chains
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Delegation is not impersonation by convention

contracts.name: Step-Up and Transaction Authorization
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Authentication strength is contextual

contracts.name: Receiver-Side Authority Is Final
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: A sender may carry claims, evidence and requested authority, but the receiving trust domain owns the final decision

contracts.name: Policy Decision / Enforcement Separation
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Centralizing policy semantics can reduce drift, but centralizing execution authority creates a crown jewel

contracts.name: Capability-Shaped Privileged Execution
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: The safest privileged executor is deliberately weak: it exposes a small vocabulary of typed, allowlisted operations instead of shell, SQL, Kubernetes-admin, or arbitrary HTTP

contracts.name: Confused Deputy Defense
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: A powerful service can be tricked into spending its own authority for a weaker caller

contracts.name: Authorization at Object, Property, and Function
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: “Endpoint requires auth” is not meaningful protection if a caller can select another tenant's object, write protected fields, or invoke an admin function through the same API model

contracts.name: Quorum and Separation of Duties
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: For high-impact actions, least privilege is insufficient if one compromised identity can both request, approve and execute

contracts.name: Policy as a Versioned Security Artifact
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Policy changes are production code changes with potentially larger blast radius than application code

contracts.name: Canonical Semantic Fingerprints
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Distributed systems need to know whether two requests are the “same” semantically, not merely byte-identical

contracts.name: Idempotency Is Not Replay Protection
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Idempotency prevents duplicate effects for a known semantic operation; replay protection prevents an attacker from reusing captured authority

contracts.name: Transport Does Not Transfer Authority
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Message buses, API gateways, signed envelopes and internal networks transport claims; they do not create business authority

contracts.name: Schema Validity Is Not Semantic Safety
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: A perfectly schema-valid request can still be malicious, unauthorized, stale, contradictory or dangerous

contracts.name: Egress Is a Privilege, Not Plumbing
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: A service with broad outbound network access can turn SSRF, prompt injection, dependency compromise or credential theft into lateral movement and exfiltration

contracts.name: Tenant Isolation Is End-to-End
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Multi-tenancy fails when only the database query is tenant-scoped but caches, queues, metrics, object stores, rate limits, audit streams or background workers are not

contracts.name: Unknown Outcome Is a First-Class State
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Distributed side effects have an uncomfortable state: the caller timed out after sending, so the effect may or may not have happened

contracts.name: Key Hierarchy with Purpose Separation
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: A flat set of “signing keys” becomes unmanageable during compromise

contracts.name: Short-Lived Credentials and Secret Zero
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Secret managers reduce sprawl but do not solve the “secret zero” problem if workloads still need a long-lived bootstrap credential to access them

contracts.name: Rotation and Revocation Are Protocols
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Generating a new key is easy; changing trust safely across distributed verifiers is the hard part

contracts.name: Cryptographic Domain Separation and Agility
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Crypto failures often come from using the right primitive in the wrong domain: same key, same hash preimage, or same signature semantics across unrelated purposes

contracts.name: Envelope Encryption and Key Scope
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: “Encrypted at rest” is too coarse

contracts.name: Cryptographic Use Is Auditable
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: A key can remain secret while still being abused by an authorized but compromised signer

contracts.name: Source Change Path Is Part of the TCB
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Artifact signing cannot rescue a malicious source change that legitimately passed through the build

contracts.name: Provenance, Not Just SBOM
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: An SBOM says what components are present; provenance says how an artifact was built, from what source and by which builder

contracts.name: Keyless Signing and Transparency
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Long-lived CI signing keys become high-value secrets exposed to workflow compromise

contracts.name: Admission by Digest and Attestation
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Scanning in CI is advisory if the runtime can deploy something else

contracts.name: Dependency Closure and Hermeticity
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Pinning top-level dependencies does not pin the build if resolvers can choose transitive versions, mutable indexes, build backends or system packages at build time

contracts.name: CI Isolation and Ephemeral Authority
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: CI executes attacker-influenced code by design

contracts.name: Security Delta Release Gates
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: A generic test suite treats all changes equally, but security risk is highly non-uniform

contracts.name: Release Set as a Security Object
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: In a multi-repository ecosystem, secure components can combine into an insecure release

contracts.name: No Ambient Kubernetes Authority
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Pods frequently inherit cluster authority they never use

contracts.name: Restricted Runtime Profile as Admission Policy
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Container hardening in YAML is brittle unless the platform rejects workloads that violate it

contracts.name: Network Policy Is Not Identity
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: IP/namespace segmentation limits reachability but does not prove who a peer is

contracts.name: Security Plane Resource Isolation
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Security controls can fail open indirectly when telemetry, analytics or untrusted workloads exhaust the CPU, DB pool, queues or threads needed for authorization, revocation and incident response

contracts.name: Runtime Drift Is a Security Signal
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Even with immutable deployments, emergency edits, compromised nodes or side-loaded files can make runtime differ from the admitted artifact

contracts.name: Sandbox the Dangerous Boundary, Not Everything
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Uniform sandboxing wastes cost; no sandboxing gives high-risk interpreters and plugins the same kernel/network privileges as ordinary services

contracts.name: Logs Are Not Authoritative Evidence
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Application logs optimize diagnosis; authoritative security evidence must survive compromise, retries, clock quirks and operator mistakes

contracts.name: Tamper Evidence Needs an Independent Anchor
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Hash chaining makes modification detectable only if an attacker cannot rewrite the entire chain and its head

contracts.name: Fail Closed by Transition, Not by Slogan
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: “Fail closed” applied indiscriminately can turn a dependency outage into a self-inflicted platform outage; “fail open” hides security bypasses

contracts.name: Compromise-Ready Recovery
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Disaster recovery restores availability; security recovery restores trustworthy authority

contracts.name: Security Chaos and Adversarial Rehearsal
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Security architecture remains theoretical until failure modes are exercised under realistic partial failure: stale keys, duplicate delivery, policy outage, forged approvals, corrupted artifacts and overloaded control planes

contracts.name: Measure Invariants, Not Vulnerability Counts
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Vulnerability counts are noisy and easy to game

contracts.name: The Model Is an Untrusted Planner
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Once an AI can call tools, the primary trust boundary is no longer “prompt vs model”; it is “probabilistic planner vs deterministic authority”

contracts.name: Least Agency and Tool Capability Firebreak
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Least privilege for agents must include least agency: even a correctly authorized agent should not have more autonomous action latitude than the task requires

contracts.name: Prompt/Context Taint and Provenance
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Indirect prompt injection works because untrusted content is interpreted in the same semantic channel as trusted instructions

contracts.name: Agent Identity Is Not Human Identity
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: An agent acting for a user is neither the user nor merely the hosting service

contracts.name: Agent Memory Is Security State
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Persistent memory can carry attacker instructions or corrupted facts across sessions, turning one injection into durable behavior change

contracts.name: Human Approval Is a Security Protocol
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Human-in-the-loop is not automatically safe

contracts.name: Agentic Supply Chain and Tool Trust
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Agents dynamically combine models, prompts, MCP/tool servers, plugins, retrieval sources and code packages

contracts.name: Agentic Budgets and Circuit Breakers
contracts.primary_failure_prevented: Autonomous loops turn small mistakes into cascading failures: repeated tool calls, recursive delegation, repeated purchases/deletes, token burn or fan-out across services
